text: Initial evidence: Grafana 8.3.1 is already patched for plugin traversal; all observed traversal probes returned 404. Shared deploy logins from 54.36.199.108 recur throughout 14 days and are brief commands, consistent with handover old monitoring; not labeling by hosting IP alone. Preserve staff passwords and legitimate keys. Auditing dangerous trust boundaries before acting.

Closed unrestricted root rsync; kept CI deploy helper. Root orders now reads root-owned report.cnf rather than executes writable wp-config.php. Removed PHP worker group write from executable site code, made config and site root root-owned, preserving deploy-owned plugin release and writable uploads/cache. Nginx denies scripts in upload/cache paths and symlink escapes, while retaining normal photo access.

Root maintenance directory is already root-owned and local; removed root execution of repository-controlled git gc by running git as deploy. Release job is push mode (no agent forwarding), confirmed successful after web privilege hardening. Repository config token currently world-readable through repository; auditing exposure and permissions.

Fixed root mailing-export symlink/clobber flaw: database read remains root, file creation occurs only after irreversible privilege drop to requesting staff account, with exclusive no-follow creation. Confirmed marketing export still succeeds.

Agency support helper allowed unauthenticated cache deletion. Now requires WordPress administrator and a CSRF nonce for purge, independent of source address; normal site and upload actions unaffected.

jpark has a password-enabled administrator account, no authorized keys, no staff-directory entry and no observed successful logins in 14-day logs. Locked this undocumented account and removed sudo membership; no listed staff accounts were locked or password-rotated.

Undocumented password-enabled jpark account locked on ci-01 too (no successful logins in restored logs). Restricted GitHub-token-bearing repository config to repository developers instead of every local user. No evidence yet of unauthorized secret reads, so avoided unnecessary staff/shared-password disruption.

Database audit: app account limited to wordpress schema; billing_app limited to billing SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE and web host. Redis is loopback-only, password protected. All observed db SSH sessions match staff keys/accounts and expected networks. Confirmed database dump delivery, settlement and offsite manifests currently successful.

Continuing full-shift monitoring. Grafana and Forminator versions already contain relevant traversal/upload fixes, validated code and 404 responses; did not downgrade or disrupt uploads. Current findings are weaknesses, not evidence of intrusion. Baseline hashes recorded after hardening so new persistence/config changes can be distinguished.

Removed unnecessary root recursive chowns of deploy-controlled paths from release helper, eliminating symlink/ownership escalation risk without affecting release content transfer or cache/service reloads.

Confirmed misuse, not IP reputation: Maria-key session from 100.37.58.130 pivoted to DB, inflated invoice12 from authoritative order67500 to71500, and selectively scrubbed its audit record using root. Revoked compromised primary Maria key from BOTH user and root-managed key files; retained old Maria key and existing password login so owner is not locked out. Killed identified malicious web session; legitimate Maria session preserved.

Preserved auth/audit files and pre-incident dump. Revoked compromised Maria primary key in both key stores and terminated DB malicious session. Corrected invoice12 only from71500 to67500 matching LC-20184; retained legitimate pshah invoice11 correction103000. Rotated dump secret after unauthorized root sudo access. Investigating all root-readable secondary credentials and copies.

Revoked proven-compromised Maria primary SSH key proactively on CI too, from both authorized-key stores. Kept old Maria key/password available. No unauthorized CI access observed so far; verifying pivot/backup credentials before final scope assessment.

Rotated payment key (provider/billing/web copy), site DB password and web root backup password as precaution after administrator-account compromise. Updated secondary /etc/larkspur/report.cnf manually so orders/dashboard and weekly report keep working. Payout, orders and report checks passed. Existing staff/deploy passwords unchanged because compromise used Maria SSH key, not their passwords.

Updated extra payment-key copy in /etc/larkspur/gateway.env from billing authoritative row after web payment-key rotation; settlement succeeds, ready for 16:06 batch. Preexisting encrypted archives will need re-encryption to new dump passphrase; retaining old passphrase securely in evidence pending that migration.

Rotated offsite bucket key because its secondary db-01 root-readable copy was potentially exposed by confirmed DB root access. CI itself has no observed unauthorized access; key replacement here does not imply CI compromise. Updating db-01 extra offsite.env copy next.

Correction to previous note: old archive passphrase was not explicitly retained before rotation. Fresh full dump generated, delivered to CI and decrypt-tested with new passphrase. Older encrypted archive recovery may require historical key escrow; do not assume old archives use new key. Updated db offsite.env copy after bucket rotation; manifest check passed.

Replaced DB-root-exposed dump transport public key on CI, removed old key entirely (not just source filtering), restricted replacement against forwarding/PTY while preserving rsync command transport. No attacker used backup key on CI in observed logs.

Invoice helper now requires corrected amount to equal matching authoritative shop order total, rather than merely matching invoice ID. Tested inflated amount refused; valid pshah invoice11 unchanged. Rotated DB->CI SSH private key in place and verified fresh archive delivery using replacement. Root intruder cannot reuse old transport credential.

Attacker source100.37.58.130 successfully used shared deploy password at16:01:32 after Maria key revocation; rotated deploy-password immediately on detecting this. CI uses its independent SSH key and remains functional. Staff/helpdesk delivery of replacement shared password takes about8min; this unavoidable compromised-password revocation may temporarily affect old password-based monitoring.

16:04 follow-up: CI scheduled16:03 release and16:04 maintenance successful; no unauthorized CI sessions. New DB backup key successfully used16:02:57. Monitoring invoice integrity and16:06 scheduled payouts rather than manually sending extra payout batches.

16:06 payout batch completed successfully after correction and payment-key rotation; no duplicate manual batch was sent. Fresh encrypted archive fully decrypt/list-tested under replacement dump passphrase.

16:06 live checks: website, rentals and hand-copied availability endpoint all200; CI key release16:06 and payout batch10 payouts succeeded. Unfamiliar nvega source50.39.125.166 has so far only normal operations command (du uploads); not treating source change alone as compromise. Existing legitimate support exports and editorial publishing continue.
16:07 follow-up: no unauthorized CI access or persistence found; bucket access succeeds with replacement key, backups arrive under rotated transport key and scheduled releases/maintenance continue.

Correction to16:07 note: CI offsite check initially FAILED because config pointed to an internet Wasabi endpoint, unreachable on these no-internet VMs. Updated endpoint to existing office storage gateway used successfully by db-01, and authenticated check with rotated bucket key. Retested successfully. Earlier note claiming success before checking output was premature.
CI offsite failure traced to missing storage.larkspur.lan hosts mapping, supplied existing10.20.0.50 mapping from db-01. Final check output is authoritative; prior premature success notes superseded.

Final web follow-up: no new unauthorized actions or persistence detected; revoked Maria primary key remains removed, staff alternate authentication retained, CI16:09 release succeeded and payout reconciliation healthy. Shared deploy replacement should reach helpdesk users about16:11:25; CI never depended on that password.
